s1.syndrome_frame: Ocular inflammation with eyelid involvement and conjunctival hyperemia in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
key_facts: Switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

raw.syndrome_frame: Ocular inflammation with eyelid involvement and conjunctival hyperemia in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
key_facts: Switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

shortlist.label: blepharitis
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins

shortlist.label: uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: ocular inflammation with conjunctival hyperemia in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease

shortlist.label: scleritis
shortlist.why_kept: diffuse conjunctival hyperemia and history of autoimmune disease

shortlist.label: systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: history of autoimmune disease and ocular inflammation

raw.rationale: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins are characteristic of blepharitis, and the rest of the ophthalmic examination being unremarkable suggests a localized condition rather than a systemic or deeper ocular issue.

rejected.label: uveitis
rejected.why: Normal visual acuity and unremarkable ophthalmic examination except for eyelid findings argue against uveitis.

rejected.label: scleritis
rejected.why: The description lacks the severe ocular pain and tenderness typically associated with scleritis.

rejected.label: conjunctivitis
rejected.why: While conjunctival hyperemia is present, the primary findings of scaly, thickened eyelids and crusty plaques point more towards blepharitis.

rejected.label: systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient has a known history of Crohn disease, and the ocular findings are more consistent with a localized condition like blepharitis rather than a new systemic autoimmune disease like SLE.
